claims.text: Our agents already have dedicated resources with a small blast radius: their own mailbox, their own code-host account, their own Claude account.
claims.quote: Our agents already have dedicated resources with a small blast radius

claims.text: The next dedicated resource is a desktop of the agent's own, and it should be a Mac, because that is where most agent desktop apps arrive first.
claims.quote: The next one is a desktop of their own, and it should be a Mac

claims.text: This is a business plan for somebody else to build; it names no provider, and the whole plan with numbers, policies and a calculator is in the Agent Desk vault.
claims.quote: This is a business plan for somebody else to build

claims.text: The owner does not run agents on his own laptop because everything he has is on it.
claims.quote: because everything I have is on it

claims.text: Windows and Linux run as virtual machines by the hour from many places and a Mac never has; that gap is the business.
claims.quote: a Mac never has been. That gap is the business.

claims.text: Apple's licence allows leasing a Mac only for the sole purpose of providing Permitted Developer Services, such as continuous integration and building software.
claims.quote: for the sole purpose of providing Permitted Developer Services

claims.text: Each lease period must be at least twenty-four consecutive hours, to one customer with sole and exclusive use and control.
claims.quote: Each lease period must be for a minimum period of twenty-four (24) consecutive hours

claims.text: Up to two additional virtual copies of macOS are allowed on a Mac you own or control, and not for time-sharing or service bureau use.
claims.quote: Up to two additional copies in virtual machines on a Mac you own or control

value.unit: additional virtual copies of macOS per Mac

claims.text: A shared pool of Macs whose desktops are rented by the minute to many customers for general agent work is not allowed.
claims.quote: So a shared pool of Macs whose desktops are rented by the minute to many customers, for general agent work, is out.

claims.text: The macOS 27 licence opens its virtualisation and leasing clauses with an exception for terms provided in writing by Apple, a route to written terms.
claims.quote: which is a route to written terms for a use Apple wants to support

claims.text: The plan recommends building a dedicated Mac run for the customer and developer agents, giving away the software, asking Apple for terms, and not building the pool.
claims.quote: build A and C, give away E, ask for D, and do not build the pool

claims.text: Per-minute pricing survives as a meter on a Mac one customer holds, never as a share of a Mac that others use.
claims.quote: Per-minute pricing survives, as a meter on a Mac one customer holds, never as a share of a Mac that others use.

claims.text: Each run boots a clean macOS, installs sgit, is given one key and clones one set-up vault; a small signed program in it does the rest.
claims.quote: Boot a clean macOS, install sgit, give it one key, and clone one set-up vault.

claims.text: The vaults divide the work like a supply chain, each party holding only its slice: set-up, code and data, a mandate vault, keys by PKI, and an audit vault.
claims.quote: The vaults divide the work, the way a supply chain should, with each party holding only its slice

claims.text: Each desktop has its own key pair and the vault keys it needs are encrypted to its public key, which is authorisation by encryption rather than by privilege.
claims.quote: Each desktop has its own key pair; the vault keys it needs are encrypted to its public key

claims.text: The bootstrap's key-handling steps were run with sgit 0.20.0 on Linux; nothing has run on a Mac yet.
claims.quote: Nothing has run on a Mac yet; the plan says so.

claims.text: For the same customer service agent, the excess over the mandate that nothing bounds is 23 rows of a 33-row grant on your own Mac, 11 on a dedicated Mac and 3 on a hardened one.
claims.quote: the excess nothing bounds falls from 23 rows to 11 to 3

value.unit: unbounded rows of the grant on your own Mac

claims.text: Of 22 hostile inputs, a boundary or an empty grant stops none on your own Mac, 2 on a dedicated Mac and 12 on a hardened one.
claims.quote: Hostile inputs stopped by a boundary or an empty grant, of 22

value.unit: hostile inputs stopped on the hardened Mac

claims.text: On your own Mac the behaviour policy is enormous because the grant is everything you have, and nothing is held by a boundary.
claims.quote: because the grant is everything you have: your mail, your files, your browser sessions, your keychain, your messages

claims.text: On a hardened Mac third-party controls do the rest: a supervised standard account, an egress proxy for the mandate's hosts, a binary allowlist, a mail gateway and every event streamed to the audit vault.
claims.quote: an egress proxy that allows only the mandate's hosts, a binary allowlist

claims.text: What is left on the hardened Mac is mostly the shop's admin screen, a finding about the shop's software, and screen recording, which a profile cannot grant.
claims.quote: That is a finding about the shop's software, not about the desktop

claims.text: For about 104 desktop hours a month, a dedicated Mac with the meter costs about £211 a month, a Mac mini run yourself about £119, and daily leases about £390.
claims.quote: a dedicated Mac with the meter costs about £211 a month

value.unit: GBP a month for a dedicated Mac with the meter

claims.text: The dedicated Mac wins once looking after your own takes more than about four hours a month, and beats daily leases once you need a Mac on more than about twelve days a month.
claims.quote: The dedicated Mac wins once looking after your own takes more than about four hours a month

claims.text: On the map, the agent's desktop moves from custom-built to product on parts that are already products or commodities: Apple silicon, the macOS virtual machine, the models, the desktop agent apps.
claims.quote: The agent's desktop moves from custom-built to product, on parts that are already products or commodities

claims.text: The plan asks a Mac host for dedicated Macs per customer with an erase API, a meter inside, a developer-agent offer, a joint approach to Apple for written terms, and an open stack.
claims.quote: A joint approach to Apple for written terms covering agent desktops

claims.text: Write the behaviour policy before the product: it is the argument, and it tells you which controls matter.
claims.quote: Write the behaviour policy before the product: it is the argument, and it tells you which controls matter.

claims.text: The plan assumes about five minutes from request to a working desktop, and the boot has not been timed yet.
claims.quote: it has not been timed yet

claims.text: Queueing many agents on one Mac satisfies one user at a time; the purpose of the lease and who the user is decide the rest.
claims.quote: Queueing satisfies "one user at a time"; the purpose of a lease, and who the user is, decide the rest.

claims.text: A queue of coding agents on a leased Mac fits the licence like a continuous integration runner; a queue of office agents is outside the lease however carefully scheduled.
claims.quote: A queue of office agents, working in mail, a browser and desktop apps, is outside the lease however carefully it is scheduled.

claims.text: If customers' own agents get slots on the operator's Mac, that is the time-sharing the licence excludes, and each customer would need a lease of at least 24 hours.
claims.quote: each of them would need a lease of their own of at least 24 hours

claims.text: The refinement: a dedicated Mac per customer is needed when the agents are the customer's; when the agents are the operator's, one Mac can serve many of them in turn.
claims.quote: When the agents are the operator's, doing work the customer buys, one Mac can serve many of them in turn

claims.text: The licence quotes are from Apple's macOS 15, 26 and 27 licences; the reading of them is ours and is not legal advice.
claims.quote: the reading of them is ours and is not legal advice

claims.text: Mac prices are from Apple's UK store on 9 October 2026; every other number is an assumption, labelled in the vault.
claims.quote: every other number is an assumption, labelled in the vault

claims.text: The article was drafted from a voice memo by Dinis Cruz by agent@riskmandate.ai, running Claude Opus 5.5, on 9 October 2026.
claims.quote: by agent@riskmandate.ai (Claude Opus 5.5, claude-opus-5-5) in the sgit.ai site session, on 9 October 2026

claims.text: Claude's desktop app and Cowork are very capable on a desktop, and Claude can drive desktop applications well: mail, messages, a browser, creative and video tools.
claims.quote: Claude's desktop app and Cowork are very capable on a desktop
